items.title: George "Jug" Jernberg Interview, 1963-08-23
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you ever hear Jimmy known him? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, very good. I was trying to think of his name just last night, I think. He had a style of clarinet playing that was very, very nice...

ctx.x: Well, yes, I liked Shields playing and Rapoli with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, or Rapolo or whatever his name was. He was all right, too. And of course, Johnny Dodds with Joe Oliver. Oh, Jesus. He was great. I thought he was wonderful.
Did you ever hear Jimmy known him?

Yes, very good. I was trying to think of his name just last night, I think. He had a style of clarinet playing that was very, very nice, very soft and subdued, but very nice clarinet playing. He used to work at the old Apex Club on 35th Street. Yes, he was a very nice clarinet player. Yes. He was a clarinet player. But I'll say this. We'll get back to Johnny Dodds again. That guy was strictly a New Orleans jazz clarinet player, but brother, his instrument always sounded like a clarinet. Yeah. Always sounded like…
